source_title: Forecasting Trends in Disability in a Super-Aging Society: Adapting the Future Elderly Model to Japan
claim_candidate: The model estimates disease transition probabilities, Japan-specific mortality rates from death certificate data, and disability measures including ADLs, IADLs, cognition, and social functioning from JSTAR.
verbatim_excerpt: Our strategy requires first estimating disease transition probabilities for diseases prevalent among Japanese middle-aged and elderly populations. We then estimate Japan-specific age-sex-specific mortality rates from Japanese death certificate data. Next, we use these health and mortality transition functions to construct a micro-simulation forecast of the health and age structure of Japan’s population over the next decades. Finally, we estimate how disabled this future population is likely to be given their health status. Our measure of disability, derived from the JSTAR survey, includes functional status measures like Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs), as well as additional measures of cognition and social functioning.

verbatim_excerpt: This study estimates a new state-transition microsimulation model – the Japanese Future Elderly Model (FEM) – for Japan.
